Karthik / team — quick legal read below (high level; aim to limit back-and-forth with Aurelia):

On Mon, Aug 15, 2027 at 08:12 AM Oliver Smith <oliver.smith@aureliatx.com> wrote:
> Top priorities for Aurelia:
> - Explicit SCCs reference and choice of Module (customer preference for updated SCCs + Module Two wording)
> - Subprocessor disclosure cadence and right to object (they want a 10-day objection window)
> - Audit scope: Aurelia prefers on-site / full-scope audits for an appointed third-party auditor
> - Data residency and handback assurances (retain only aggregated logs after contract end)

My recommended positions (short bullets you can send to customer):
- SCCs: agree to incorporate the EU Commission SCCs (2021) as an addendum, but use Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) only where the EU SCCs text is applicable to this relationship. We should not accept modifications to the SCCs themselves.
- Subprocessors: provide a 30-day notification window for new subprocessors and a right to object limited to data protection risk grounds. We cannot accept a 10-day blanket objection window — operationally infeasible and risky. Offer an SLA to expedite disclosure for high-risk subprocessors.
- Audits: decline on-site full-scope audits. Offer a third-party SOC2-type report and an annual compliance package plus targeted remote evidence (logs, configurations). If the customer requires on-site audit, it must be a negotiated additional service (billable, scoped, and subject to confidentiality safeguards).
- Handback / data return: standard handback: return customer data on request within 30 days and then delete remaining PII within 90 days, with an option for extended retention by mutual agreement. Preserve minimal logs for troubleshooting and abuse prevention (retention and safeguards documented).
- Liability / indemnities: preserve existing caps in MSA — any proposal to expand unlimited liability for GDPR infringements needs escalation to legal leadership; propose we accept narrowly tailored indemnities tied to processor obligations only.

Action items:
- I will draft a concise counter-bullet summary to send to Aurelia today.
- Rishi: confirm whether we want to offer an on-site audit add-on price or only remote evidence.
- Markus: share any precedent TIA handback language from Dedicated/private customers.

Neha
Neha Kapoor | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Oliver — thanks for the redlines and the clear priorities. Per internal counsel, here's a pragmatic roadmap we can follow to reach agreement next week: 

1) SCCs: we will incorporate the EU Commission 2021 SCCs as an addendum (we cannot accept edits to the SCC text). We'll reference Module Two language where appropriate for controller-to-processor flows.
2) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide an advance notice of new subprocessors and a 30-day window to object on narrowly defined data protection risk grounds. For high-risk subprocessors we can accelerate disclosure; we will document an expedited review SLA.
3) Audits: our standard compliance deliverable is an annual independent SOC2 report + targeted remote evidence package. On-site/third-party auditor access will be considered only as a paid, scoped add-on (procurement/operational cost applies).
4) Handback: standard handback and deletion timelines — return within 30 days; delete PII within 90 days unless an extension is mutually agreed in writing. Minimal operational logs will be retained for debuggability and security; we'll specify retention limits in the TIA.
5) Liability: we'll preserve caps in the MSA; any expansion for GDPR-related fines requires escalated legal approval.

Next steps and ask from Aurelia: please confirm whether this approach is acceptable in principle. If yes, we will: (a) upload a redline that applies the SCCs + the TIA handback language to the shared drive, (b) solicit Aurelia's acceptance on the subprocessor timing and audit mechanism, and (c) route a negotiated add-on for any on-site audit scope.

Attached: Redlines_summary.xlsx (high level mapping of Aurelia asks to our positions). I can also push a tracked-change redline to the drive today if you want to review the textual edits.

Best,
Karthik
